newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Williams deal shows focus.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Williams deal shows focus.

text.p: Williams Holdings Plc said on Wednesday its sale of 15 mainly UK businesses to management demonstrated its increased focus, while at the same time showing added shareholder value.

"We have been developing the consistently narrowing focus of Williams to fire protection and security," chief executive Roger Carr told Reuters in an interview. He said the 360 million pounds sale of businesses such as Swish and Rawlplug involved UK-orientated small businesses, which would flourish elsewhere.
At the same time, the deal generated some 90 million pounds of net cash to help fund acquisitions, he said.

Williams said the group would make an exceptional gain of over 246 million pounds on the deal. Carr said that on Williams' calculations the businesses had delivered a return of 13 percent since their various acquisitions, ahead of the cost of capital.

Carr said Williams' overall target for rate of return was 12 to 15 percent. "If you can achieve that you are doing pretty well in the economic environment -- and you never expose the full value until you sell the businesses," he said.
Williams is reinvesting 57 million pounds to take a 26 percent stake in the buyout company, Newmond Ltd, which Carr said was led by a "highly-respected management team".

Carr said the company, which as an international manufacturing group has sought to shrug off the image of a conglomerate, had a number of acquisition opportunities in mind, "some of which we are looking at seriously."
He said the company, which has spent 230 million pounds on nine acquisitions this year, looked at opportunites in the Far East, Europe and North America.
"Relevance is the key rather than size -- we have three good divisions which we will build on," he said.
On current trading, Carr said the economic outlook remained challenging in Europe and warned about the strength of sterling.
On sterling, Carr said, "this year management action has meant the impact had been very limited."
He said he was encouraged by the fall in the pound over the past 24 hours, but said if the strength were maintained, conditions would be challenging.
The cash inflow of 303 million pounds from Wednesday's sale leaves the company with effective gearing of zero.
